claim: An internal 'code correctness direction' extracted by contrasting hidden states of correct vs incorrect code for the same task outperforms both log-likelihood ranking and the model's own verbalized confidence at identifying correct code.
stance_target: The proposed pivot's premise that no prior code-LLM work has already compared internal/hidden-state signals against verbalized confidence
scope_conditions: 4 open code LLMs; whole-program/whole-solution granularity, not per-test or per-requirement
quoted_support: we show that exploiting this extracted correctness representation outperforms standard log-likelihood ranking, as well as verbalized model confidence.

claim: The correctness representation is identified by contrasting mean hidden states between pairs of correct and incorrect code generated for the same programming task, analogous to prior 'truthfulness direction' work in general LLM interpretability.
stance_target: method used for internal correctness signal extraction
quoted_support: Inspired by findings that LLMs internally encode concepts like truthfulness, this paper explores if LLMs similarly represent code correctness. Specifically, we identify a correctness representation inside LLMs by contrasting the hidden states between pairs of correct and incorrect code for the same programming tasks.

claim: The extracted internal correctness signal can select higher-quality code samples without requiring test execution, demonstrating a downstream utility use case for whole-program internal correctness probing.
stance_target: downstream utility of internal code-correctness probes
scope_conditions: whole-program sample selection, not per-requirement targeting
quoted_support: we explore how this internal correctness signal can be used to select higher-quality code samples, without requiring test execution.

claim: This paper operates at whole-solution granularity (one correctness label per generated program) and does not decompose correctness into per-unit-test or per-requirement outcomes, nor does it train the model to natively verbalize calibrated per-requirement confidence.
stance_target: Per-requirement (per-unit-test) hidden-state probing of code correctness remains unclaimed territory
scope_conditions: inferred from abstract and paper framing; no per-test/per-requirement breakdown reported
quoted_support: we show that exploiting this extracted correctness representation outperforms standard log-likelihood ranking, as well as verbalized model confidence.
